sections.heading: Passing, night driving and age-related driving
sections.markdown:
# Passing, night driving and age-related driving

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
A steady do-not-walk signal tells a pedestrian not to begin crossing toward that signal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
A flashing do-not-walk signal forbids starting a crossing but lets a pedestrian already crossing continue to the nearest safe area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
A steady walk signal permits pedestrians to begin crossing toward it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian in a marked crosswalk or crossing with a walk or green signal has priority over a turning vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A01
A driver turning right on red must yield to pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A01
Be ready to stop for a person in the roadway even when the person crosses somewhere improper. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A01
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because it may hide a crossing pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A01
Approach a stopped vehicle cautiously and be ready for a person in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A01
Slow near people walking or children playing beside the roadway and allow room for an unexpected movement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian should check left, right and left again before crossing and continue watching traffic during the crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian using a guide dog or a white cane, with or without a red tip, must be given priority. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A02
Use extra care when turning or reversing near a pedestrian with a visual impairment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A02
Do not stop inside a crosswalk or obstruct the sidewalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A02
Do not honk at a pedestrian with a visual impairment because the noise can startle or confuse the person. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A02
Before turning right on red, check carefully for pedestrians and other traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A02
A phone can distract visually by drawing the eyes away, manually by occupying the hands and cognitively by diverting attention. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A02
If a call is necessary, have a passenger make it or pull off safely and stop before calling. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A02
Do not take notes or search for telephone numbers while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A02
Let incoming calls go to voicemail instead of responding while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A03
The guide describes a Louisiana prohibition on operating a wireless device while driving unless use is hands free. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A03
The guide prohibits writing, sending or reading a text communication while operating a vehicle regardless of the driver’s age. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A03
The guide prohibits accessing, reading or posting to a social-networking site while operating a vehicle regardless of age. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A03
The guide directs the reader to Louisiana Revised Statute 32:59 for exceptions to its wireless-device restrictions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A03
Peer pressure can encourage unsafe speed, illegal maneuvers, careless steering or distractions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A03
Turning to talk to passengers, racing and treating the roadway as a playground are unsafe behaviors described in the guide. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A04
Peers can improve safety by warning a driver of a mistake and encouraging safer choices. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A04
The guide recommends understanding personal limits and choosing safer travel conditions as driving abilities change. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A04
Ask a clinician or pharmacist to review medicines that might interfere with driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A04
Use required glasses or contact lenses and keep vision and hearing checked. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A04
When possible, select daylight travel and favorable weather. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A04
Plan the route in advance and favor well-lit streets, controlled left turns and straightforward parking. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A04
Maintain generous following space and avoid in-vehicle distractions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A04
A refresher course can help a driver update skills and knowledge. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-R34 | anchor: A04
When driving is no longer suitable, consider traveling with a friend or using public transportation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]
